title: MoEngage reports unauthorised access to part of its cloud infrastructure via a compromised third-party vendor account
date_note: Date is Inc42's publication day; the article says MoEngage claims it identified and contained the incident in late October. No disclosure date is given.
geo_basis: headquarters as stated by Inc42 (Bengaluru and San Francisco)
summary: Inc42 reports that MoEngage, a SaaS company, suffered unauthorised access to a limited part of its cloud infrastructure through a compromised third-party vendor account. MoEngage says it contained the incident in late October and that fewer than 1% of customer accounts were affected, each notified directly. Inc42, citing an ET report, says some customers reportedly could not access the platform for nearly seven days; MoEngage says there was no disruption to its services.
plain: A marketing software company says someone got into part of its cloud systems through a vendor's account. It says fewer than 1% of customer accounts were affected and they were told directly.
exec: A supplier-account compromise at a SaaS vendor reached customer accounts; the company and a report differ on whether service was disrupted.
action: If you are a MoEngage customer, check for MoEngage's direct notice, and ask it what was affected in your account.

validation.note: Inc42 only; it relays MoEngage's statement and an ET report it does not link. No MoEngage notice found in a web search.

review.note: Compared title, summary, date_note, fewer-than-1% figure, late-October containment, ET nearly-seven-days claim and Bengaluru/San Francisco HQ against the Inc42 article of 21 Nov; single-source status is correct
